text:
marta: Heads up — got a flood of GPU pod evictions in eu-west1 last night right after the autoscaler consolidation rollout. ~40 pods across 6 deployments.

oscar: ugh. any obvious error? eviction reason? pod status?

marta: eviction reason = NodePressure on memory for some, but a lot show 'evicted due to taint: node.k8s.io/consolidate=true:NoSchedule' after the drain step. suspect the consolidation taint was added by the new scale-down logic. logs attached in CI link: https://internal.logs/replay/2334

jen: can you paste the node list / taint output? also which nodepool? eu-gpu-consolidate-pool?

marta: yup, pool = eu-gpu-consolidate-pool. quick dump:

```
$ kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=eu-gpu-consolidate-pool -o wide
NAME           STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    GPU
gpu-eu-12      Ready    <none>   12d   v1.26.3   10.2.1.12      a100
gpu-eu-13      Ready    <none>   11d   v1.26.3   10.2.1.13      a100
gpu-eu-14      Ready    <none>   5d    v1.26.3   10.2.1.14      a100

affinity/taints:
$ kubectl describe node gpu-eu-12 | grep -A2 Taints
Taints: node.k8s.io/consolidate=true:NoSchedule

the autoscaler added that taint during the scale-down pre-drain. pods with soft affinity lost their place and were evicted.\n```

kai: Did the drain respect PodDisruptionBudgets? Autoscaler should check PDBs before adding a consolidate taint.

samir: I think the new algorithm adds taint early to mark for consolidation, then drains. If the drain errors, taint stays and scheduler refuses to place new pods back, causing churn.

k8s-autoscaler-bot: scaledown: node gpu-eu-12 removed (terminated) by scale-down controller at 2026-03-03T19:02:13Z, because underutilized for 12m

oscar: that explains the immediate term evictions. but why did churn continue for 2 hours? Shouldn't it rebalance?

marta: we saw a race: a few deployments had nodeSelector: gpu-type=a100 and preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity to GPU model. After nodes removed, remaining nodes matched but the new taint prevented placement, and the scheduler repeatedly retried, triggering backoff, leaving replicas down until the taint was removed manually.

jen: any metric spikes? I noticed cost went up in the same window.

marta: cost profile: short-term increase in preemptible/spot instance fallback in us-west as requests spilled. Also we had increased API retries from user services which bumped egress.

samir: repro steps for local run? I can try to simulate quickly.

marta: steps I ran:
1) scale pool down from 6->3 via autoscaler sim flag
2) autoscaler adds taint node.k8s.io/consolidate=true:NoSchedule to candidates
3) drains nodes
4) drain failed on 2 nodes due to failed PDB checks (ignored by code path)
5) taint not cleared, scheduler won't place pods back -> eviction cascade

samir: ok will try with a patch to clear taint on drain failure.

kai: patch idea: only add taint after drain successfully completed, or attach ephemeral annotation and only convert to taint post-checks. less blast radius.

oscar: agree. short-term mitigation: manual removal of taint on nodes and force re-schedule:

```
kubectl taint nodes gpu-eu-12 node.k8s.io/consolidate- --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deployment -l app=llm-worker -n inference
```

jen: can we also add an alert: if autoscaler taint applied && drain not completed in 5m -> rollback taint? create an SLO for node-level drains.

marta: good call. I'll open an urgent PR: 1) change order (drain -> taint) 2) add rollback on failure 3) add alert on taint-without-drain

ops-bot: incident created: #inc-2026-0303-eu-gpu-evictions assigned to @marta @samir

oscar: thanks. also let's add an e2e for PDB-respecting scale-down. that would have caught this.

marta: noted. will add tests and a new canary run in staging. will post PR link shortly.

kai: also flagging for capacity planning: consolidation pool might have too few distinct AZs, making re-scheduling slower due to AZ skew. consider cross-az allocation or draining more conservatively.

marta: yup. follow-ups: PR + alert + postmortem. I can draft the postmortem if ops + eng-platform want to collab.

jen: i'll help with the postmortem and add cost impact numbers. thanks for catching this early.

samir: I'll queue the quick patch now (clear taint on failure). will ping here when merged.

marta: thanks all. I'll update thread with PR and timeline.\n
